title: NY State Assembly · District 47
area: Southwestern Brooklyn, including Bensonhurst, Gravesend, Bath Beach, Dyker Heights and Midwood.

context.text: Incumbent William Colton has represented this district since first winning election in November 1996. Both the Democratic and Republican/Conservative primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled, so Colton and John Ricottone advanced to the general election without appearing on a primary ballot. A third potential Republican/Conservative candidate, Karina Bertaeva, withdrew or was disqualified before the primary.

priorities.text: Quality-of-life and neighborhood issues, including opposition to a proposed homeless shelter at 2501 86th Street and to an MTA B82 Select Bus Service plan.
Public safety, including opposition to reducing NYPD funding.
Education funding and preserving the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT) and gifted-and-talented programs.

positions.summary: Cosponsored A1466, the New York Health Act (2025–26 session), which would create a universal single-payer health plan (New York Health) for state residents.

record.text: Sponsored A1994, which would allow certain defenses to parking violations despite entry of a default judgment; the bill passed the Assembly on April 28, 2026 and was delivered to the Senate, where it was referred to committee.
Sponsored A9290, which would require silent alarms to be installed in classrooms across all public, charter and private schools in New York State; the bill remains in committee.
Serves on the Correction, Environmental Conservation, Governmental Employees, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees in the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: John Ricottone

priorities.text: Public safety, including repealing New York's bail reform law so that people he describes as violent repeat offenders are kept in jail.
Affordability, saying the cost of food, gas and electricity has forced some families to cut other spending to cover bills.
Education, saying children are not being taught to read and write as well as they should be.

candidates.researchNotes: Ricottone has not previously held elected office, so he has no official voting or bill-sponsorship record. His positions and background are drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no separate campaign website could be located. None of his stated priorities maps cleanly onto a documented stance on the fixed issue list without inferring beyond what he said.
